subject: Order Form IP liability — defend assignment vs. reimbursement and notice cadence
messages:
From: Clarke Patel <c.patel@nexenta.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrea Ruiz <andrea@legal-nexenta.com>, Nexenta Contracts <contracts@nexenta.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form IP liability language — ask re: defend vs reimburse

Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of open items on the order form: specifically the third-party IP claim language. Our legal team is proposing a single line: Redwood will defend and hold harmless Nexenta for third-party claims alleging infringement arising from use of the Service.

We attached a marked redline (Nexenta_OrderForm_redline_05012028.docx). Before we circulate internally we need confirmation on two practical points so procurement can proceed:

- Will Redwood accept the right-to-defend/control for all third-party IP claims tied to Nexenta’s use of the Service (including model outputs generated by prompts)?
- If Redwood declines, will you accept a reimbursement framework with clear remedy cap and notice/evidence timelines?

Can you confirm Redwood’s position and any standard alternative you typically offer? We’re on a tight procurement window and would like to close next week.

—Clarke
Clarke Patel
Senior Counsel, Nexenta Systems

Subject: Re: Order form IP liability language — ask re: defend vs reimburse

Clarke — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Looping in our legal and contracts leads (Kimberly and Laura) to respond with a concrete proposal.

Quick operational questions for your side to help us draft a narrow compromise:
- Do you expect the clause to cover outputs that Nexenta users generate by pasting third-party content into prompts (prompt-derived alleged infringements)?
- What is the procurement target cap for liability/remedy you are comfortable with (e.g., 12x subscription or a fixed dollar floor)?

We’ll aim to get a redline back by EOD (PT).

Thanks,
Sean
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Clarke Patel <c.patel@nexenta.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Andrea Ruiz <andrea@legal-nexenta.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form IP liability language — ask re: defend vs reimburse

Hi all — I reviewed Nexenta’s proposed redline and sketched a practical middle path that addresses procurement risk while protecting Redwood’s operational exposure. Attaching our marked response (Redwood_response_redline_05212028.docx). Below is a summary of the compromise and operational mechanics we’d propose: 

1) Scope split (clean, actionable):
   - Redwood will defend and control third-party claims that allege infringement arising from the Service itself (i.e., the model implementation, weights, and hosted model artifacts that we ship and manage).
   - For claims that arise solely from Customer-supplied inputs or outputs generated by Customer prompts ("prompt-derived outputs"), Redwood will offer reimbursement of documented settlement/judgment costs up to a capped amount per Order Form (see remedy cap language), provided Customer gives timely notice and cooperates.

2) Notice/evidence timeline:
   - Customer must provide written notice to Redwood within 30 days of receiving a claim; failure to provide timely notice is a defense-limiting factor.
   - Redwood may require (and Customer must provide) reasonable technical evidence (examples of prompt, output, event logs) to evaluate whether the claim implicates the Service core vs. customer content.

3) Defense control & participation:
   - Where Redwood defends, Redwood will have the right to select counsel and control the defense, with Customer reasonable participation rights.
   - If Redwood does not control the defense (e.g., reimbursement path), Customer must obtain Redwood’s consent (not unreasonably withheld) for settlement terms that admit liability or obligate Redwood beyond the cap.

4) Remedy cap and insurance: 
   - Proposed cap: greater of (i) 12x monthly subscription fees for the applicable Order Form term or (ii) $750,000.
   - Customer to maintain commercially reasonable E&O/cyber insurance (industry standard limits) and notify Redwood of material changes. This is to ensure the reimbursement path is actionable.

5) Carveouts and red flags:
   - Carve out from defense obligation: claims based on Customer’s deliberate misuse (malicious actor usage), prompt engineering designed to reproduce third-party proprietary content, or where Customer declines to cooperate.

Rationale: The split preserves customer-facing coverage for defects in our model/service while reasonably limiting exposure where the alleged infringement flows from customer inputs or user-generated content. Happy to iterate — if Nexenta needs a single, bright-line approach we can also propose a unified defend-with-cap model (i.e., Redwood defends but financial exposure capped as above).

Next steps: Laura and I can draft the specific Order Form language reflecting this split and circulate for Nexenta procurement review. Please confirm if 30-day notice and the proposed cap are workable for you.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form IP liability language — ask re: defend vs reimburse

Kimberly/Sean —

Appreciate the detailed write-up. A couple of procurement comments from our side after an internal check:

- The prompt-derived output carveout is a hard sell for our security and product teams — our customers expect the Service to carry defend obligations for outputs that result from normal product use.
- We cannot accept a 30-day notice in all cases; procurement prefers 45 days given legal intake processes for some of our EU customers.
- The proposed cap level is directionally OK but we need a floor for smaller engagements (e.g., $1M floor) to avoid numeric surprises for purchasing approvers.

If Redwood can move to: (i) single defend obligation for third-party IP claims tied to Customer use of the Service (no prompt carveout), (ii) 45-day notice, and (iii) cap equal to greater of 12x monthly or $1M, we can proceed toward signatures this week.

If you cannot accept (i), please propose an operational workaround (e.g., escrow of representative prompt logs + a binding dispute queuing step) that mitigates procurement concerns.

—Clarke
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Clarke Patel <c.patel@nexenta.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form IP liability language — ask re: defend vs reimburse

Clarke — thanks for the prompt feedback. Internally, Kimberly and I discussed your proposals and prepared a short negotiation playbook attached (Negotiation_Playbook_ND-3291.pdf) plus a clean Order Form option that implements the hybrid compromise (Proposed_OrderForm_Solution_05232028.docx). Summary of our final ask / offer: 

- Redwood will accept a single defend obligation for third-party IP claims tied to Customer use of the Service IF Nexenta accepts the following operational guardrails: 
  1) Remedy cap = greater of (i) 12x monthly fees or (ii) $1,000,000;
  2) Notice = 35 days (compromise between 30/45);
  3) Customer must provide technical evidence (prompts, outputs, logs) within 14 days of request and cooperate in discovery;
  4) Carveout remains for deliberate misuse or actions to intentionally replicate third-party content;
  5) Customer to carry E&O/cyber insurance with a $2M minimum and notify Redwood if limits change.

Why this is reasonable: it preserves a customer-facing defend commitment while setting commercial limits and operational steps that let Redwood triage claims quickly (which helps both parties avoid protracted litigation costs).

If Nexenta can sign to these guardrails, we’ll update the Order Form language and route for countersignature today. If you need a different notice period, we can discuss a regionally scoped variance for EU deals, but we prefer a consistent global baseline.

Please advise — we’re standing by to turn the doc around.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
